phases.title: Foundations
phases.description: Build accounting literacy — read a P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow statement, and trace how money moves through a business.

phases.title: Financial Statement Analysis & Ratios
phases.description: Go beyond reading the statements to interrogating them: decompose ROE with DuPont analysis, normalize statements with common-size and trend analysis, and analyze cash flow through the working-capital cycle.

phases.title: Markets & Instruments
phases.description: Understand the instruments (equity, debt, derivatives) and the players — how sell-side and buy-side firms differ.

phases.title: Corporate Finance
phases.description: Learn how firms fund themselves and choose investments — capital structure, WACC, capital budgeting, working capital.

phases.title: Advanced Accounting I: Revenue, Leases & Tax
phases.description: The accounting mechanics FMVA calls out as advanced: multi-step revenue recognition, on-balance-sheet leases, and the deferred-tax and stock-comp lines that quietly move every forecast.

phases.title: Advanced Accounting II: Consolidation & Complex Entities
phases.description: How a group of companies becomes one set of financial statements: consolidation and the equity method, the goodwill an acquisition creates and when it breaks, pensions, and the GAAP/IFRS/Ind AS differences an analyst has to reconcile.

phases.title: Budgeting, Forecasting & Cash Flow Planning
phases.description: Build the planning toolkit CFI's FMVA core assumes: budgeting approaches and the annual cycle, short-term 13-week and monthly cash-flow forecasting, and scenario and sensitivity analysis for stress-testing a model's assumptions.

phases.title: Financial Modelling Fundamentals & Best Practice
phases.description: Learn how professional models are actually built: structure and design conventions, driver-based revenue and cost forecasts, the supporting schedules that feed a 3-statement model, and how to handle circularity and audit a model for errors.

phases.title: Dashboards & Financial Data Visualization
phases.description: Turn analysis into something a decision-maker can act on: data visualization principles for financial reporting, and building interactive dashboards in Excel with charts, KPIs, and variance views.

phases.title: Equity Research & Valuation
phases.description: Go deep on the analyst's toolkit — build a DCF from discount-rate first principles, run a rigorous comps screen, and use precedent transactions and trading multiples to triangulate an enterprise value.

phases.title: Advanced Valuation Technique
phases.description: The technical layer most courses skip: bridging enterprise value to equity value with the treasury stock method, choosing and applying terminal value methods correctly with mid-year and stub-period conventions, and synthesizing methods into a football field.

phases.title: Advanced Financial Modeling
phases.description: Go beyond reading statements — build a fully integrated 3-statement model from scratch, layer in acquisition debt with an LBO model, and analyze credit risk the way a lender does.

phases.title: Fixed Income Analytics
phases.description: Price a bond off its cash flows, measure how its price moves when rates move, and read the spread between it and a risk-free benchmark as the market's own estimate of default risk.

phases.title: Credit Ratings & Loan Documentation
phases.description: How a rating agency actually assigns a letter grade, and what a credit agreement's covenants really let a lender do when a borrower deteriorates — the two pieces of the credit toolkit fin-p8's ratio-and-covenant-headroom work assumes but does not itself teach.

phases.title: Investment Banking & M&A
phases.description: Learn how deals are structured and value is created or destroyed — synergies, due diligence, post-merger integration.

phases.title: Private Equity & Alternative Investments
phases.description: Explore the buy-side beyond public markets — how private equity funds source and structure deals, how hedge funds generate returns across strategies, and how venture capital evaluates early-stage bets.

phases.title: Quantitative Portfolio Management
phases.description: The buy-side quant toolkit: price risk and return with CAPM and factor models, attribute a portfolio's performance to the decisions that drove it, and use regression, simulation and tail-risk measures to know what could go wrong.

phases.title: Leveraged Finance, Credit & Restructuring
phases.description: The debt side of the deal, and what happens when it goes wrong: the leveraged product set, how credit agreements actually constrain a borrower, and the in- and out-of-court routes through distress.

phases.title: Private Credit, Distressed & Special Situations
phases.description: Buying and holding debt rather than advising on it: bilateral lending that never gets syndicated, and investing in claims on companies in trouble.

phases.title: Structured Finance & Derivatives
phases.description: Understand how assets are pooled and tranched into securities, how options and Greeks govern hedging decisions, and how interest-rate and credit derivatives reshape risk across a portfolio.

phases.title: Derivatives Pricing & Real Options
phases.description: Beyond the Greeks and CDS mechanics already covered: how forwards, futures and swaps are actually priced off no-arbitrage, how an option's price is built up on a binomial tree or in closed form, and how the same option logic prices flexibility inside a capital project.

phases.title: Corporate Treasury & Risk Management
phases.description: The treasury seat's job: keep the company liquid day to day, hedge the FX and interest-rate exposures the business creates just by operating, and decide which risks are worth paying to remove.

phases.title: Specialised Coverage & Asset-Class Modelling
phases.description: Where the standard model breaks. A bank has no EBITDA and no free cash flow; a building is priced on NOI and a cap rate; a toll road is a debt-sizing exercise with no terminal value. Each needs its own mental model.

phases.title: Real Estate Finance & Deal Modelling
phases.description: Underwrite and model real property deals beyond REIT-level analysis: acquisitions, ground-up development, debt sizing and the promote structures that split profit between sponsors and investors.

phases.title: Natural Resources: Mining, Oil & Gas Modelling
phases.description: Model extractive-industry assets, where value comes from a depleting reserve rather than a growing business: mining NAV off a metal price deck, and oil & gas NAV off production decline curves.

phases.title: Renewables, Power & Infrastructure Deal Modelling
phases.description: Model contracted-cash-flow assets beyond the single project finance topic in fin-p14-t3: renewable power projects priced off a PPA and capacity factor, non-recourse debt sculpted to a target DSCR, and infrastructure PPPs paid on availability rather than usage.

phases.title: Growth-Industry & Consumer Sector Modelling
phases.description: Build the revenue engine right for four industries that do not run on a standard operating model: SaaS (cohorts and recurring revenue), marketplaces (GMV and take rate), restaurants/retail (unit economics and comps), and biotech (a drug pipeline valued on probability of success, not certainty).

phases.title: Advanced M&A Deal Modelling
phases.description: Push the LBO (fin-p8-t2) and merger model (fin-p5-t3) skills to what a PE associate or M&A banker actually builds on the job: a multi-tranche capital structure with a full returns-attribution bridge, mental-math paper LBOs, purchase price allocation and pro-forma consolidation, and the SOTP/contribution/fairness-opinion toolkit used on complex deals.

phases.title: PE & VC Fund Modelling and Deal Mechanics
phases.description: Move from a single deal to the fund wrapper around it: build the fund-level cash flow model that produces the J-curve, calculate the return metrics LPs actually track (beyond the waterfall concepts already covered in fin-p9-t4), and master the cap table math — dilution, option pools and liquidation preferences — behind every VC term sheet.

phases.title: Forensic Financial Analysis
phases.description: Look past the headline numbers — detect earnings manipulation through accruals analysis, identify off-balance-sheet exposure hidden in SPVs, and spot the red flags that preceded the biggest accounting scandals.

phases.title: Macro, ESG & Professional Standards
phases.description: The context every number above sits inside: the macro cycle that moves rates and spreads, the ESG factors now built into mainstream investment processes, and the ethical code that governs the profession itself.

phases.title: Financial Communication & Presenting Finance
phases.description: The skill that decides whether good analysis changes a decision: structuring a financial narrative, writing with the clarity finance leaders expect, and building and delivering the deck that presents it.

phases.title: Applied
phases.description: Apply it all to real filings and mock deals — read 10-Ks/10-Qs, practice deal exercises, prep for finance interviews.

topics.title: Reading the Three Statements
topics.description: Learn what each of the three statements reports and how they lock together: net income flows to retained earnings, and the cash flow statement reconciles accrual profit back to cash. The literacy everything later assumes.

steps.d: Say what each statement measures and over what period.
Follow a sale from revenue through receivables to cash collected.
Start from net income and rebuild the cash flow statement's operating section.

topics.title: Accounting Fundamentals
topics.description: Understand the accrual mechanics behind the numbers — revenue recognition, matching, depreciation, deferred taxes, working capital — and where management judgement enters. This is what separates reading a statement from trusting it.

steps.d: Work an example where the two diverge and explain why.
Book revenue recognition, prepaid expenses and depreciation by hand.
Pick a filing and list three policy choices management could have made differently.

topics.title: Time Value of Money & Discounting
topics.description: Money today is worth more than money later, and every valuation in this course rests on that. Present and future value, compounding, annuities and perpetuities, and the discount rate as the price of waiting.

steps.d: Grow a sum at a rate over n periods and see the curve bend.
Bring a future cash flow to today, then flex the rate and watch the value move.
Price an annuity and a perpetuity from first principles.
Discount a three-year forecast by hand — this is a DCF in miniature.

topics.title: Instruments: Equities, Debt & Derivatives
topics.description: Work through the three instrument families — equity, debt, derivatives — and what each one is a claim on, how it is issued, and what drives its price.

steps.d: Place equity, debt and derivatives on a seniority and payoff map.
Track a share and a bond from issuer to investor.
Name the two or three variables that move each instrument most.

topics.title: The Industry Map: Buy-Side vs Sell-Side
topics.description: Map the industry: who manages capital and who intermediates it, how banks, asset managers, hedge funds and research desks make money, and which seat does which work.

steps.d: List who raises capital, who allocates it, and who advises.
Trace one order from a buy-side PM through a sell-side desk.
Write what a day looks like in two roles you might actually want.

topics.title: Risk, Return & Portfolio Construction
topics.description: Risk and return as a pair: diversification, correlation, beta and the risk-free rate, then how asset allocation turns them into a portfolio. These primitives feed the cost of equity in the next phase.

steps.d: Compute volatility and correlation for two assets and combine them.
Build a two- and then five-asset portfolio and watch risk fall faster than return.
Write a policy mix for one stated objective and defend the weights.

topics.title: The Map of Finance: Coverage vs Product Groups
topics.description: Where the seats actually are inside a bank: industry coverage versus product groups (M&A, leveraged finance, ECM/DCM, restructuring), and the financial sponsors desk that sits between the bank and private equity.

steps.d: Work out who originates a deal and who executes it.
Take one announced transaction and name every group that touched it.
Why FSG is the strongest feeder into private equity.
Choose two groups you would actually recruit for and justify it.

topics.title: Cost of Capital & WACC
topics.description: Build a discount rate from its parts: cost of equity via CAPM, after-tax cost of debt, and the market-value weights between them. You learn the formula here; the valuation phase stress-tests it inside a live DCF.

steps.d: Assemble CAPM from risk-free rate, beta and equity risk premium.
Get to an after-tax cost of debt and justify the tax shield.
Combine at market values, then flex beta and see WACC move.

topics.title: Capital Structure & Capital Budgeting
topics.description: How a firm decides what to fund and how to fund it: NPV and IRR project selection, the debt-versus-equity trade-off, and working capital policy.

steps.d: Compute NPV and IRR on the same cash flows and explain where they disagree.
Argue debt versus equity for one firm on cost, flexibility and risk.
Build a cash conversion cycle and say what shortening it is worth.

topics.title: DCF Deep Dive
topics.description: Go beyond a basic DCF — build a rigorous WACC from scratch, stress-test terminal value assumptions with sensitivity tables, and understand why terminal value typically drives 60–80% of valuation output.

steps.d: Build unlevered FCF off the operating model.
Rebuild WACC for this company, not a textbook one.
Compute it both ways and show what share of value it carries.
Run a WACC-versus-growth grid and state the range you would defend.

topics.title: Comparable Company Analysis (Comps)
topics.description: Screen and select a peer group, calculate EV/EBITDA, P/E, and EV/Revenue multiples consistently across companies, and build a football-field valuation range.

steps.d: Pick a comp set and write the criteria that admitted each one.
Put everyone on the same fiscal basis and use LTM or NTM consistently.
Compute EV/EBITDA, P/E and EV/Revenue, then benchmark on median not mean.

topics.title: Precedent Transactions & Control Premiums
topics.description: Distinguish trading comps (current market prices) from deal comps (acquisition premiums baked in), and use precedent transactions to anchor the control premium in a negotiated sale.

steps.d: Build a precedent set filtered on sector, size and vintage.
Back out the control premium implied by each transaction.
Explain why deal comps sit above trading comps and when they shouldn't.

topics.title: 3-Statement Modeling
topics.description: Build a fully linked income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow statement in Excel from scratch — the foundational build behind every advanced model, versus just reading one.

steps.d: Build an assumptions block and forecast the income statement off it.
Link the cash flow statement so the balance sheet balances with no plug.
Change one driver and find every cell that should have moved.

topics.title: Credit Analysis & Debt Schedules
topics.description: Analyze a borrower the way a lender does — leverage and coverage ratios, covenant headroom — and build a debt schedule with interest, amortization, and cash sweep mechanics.

steps.d: Compute leverage, interest coverage and fixed-charge coverage on a real borrower.
Find headroom and the EBITDA decline that breaches.
Model each tranche with interest, amortisation and sweep, circularity handled.

topics.title: LBO Modeling
topics.description: Model a leveraged buyout end to end: sources & uses, acquisition debt tranches, cash sweeps, and the return math (IRR/MOIC) private equity firms underwrite deals on.

steps.d: Fund a purchase price and reconcile to the entry equity cheque.
Tranche the capital structure and run interest and mandatory amortisation.
Pay down with free cash flow, then exit and solve IRR and MOIC.
Flex entry multiple, leverage and exit multiple in a returns grid.

topics.title: The M&A Deal Process & Due Diligence
topics.description: The deal from mandate to close: buyer outreach, LOI, confirmatory diligence and signing, plus what diligence actually interrogates across financial, legal and commercial workstreams.

steps.d: Lay out mandate, marketing, LOI, diligence, signing and close with who drives each.
Pull a checklist and mark the ten items that would kill a deal.
Pick a collapsed deal and identify where in the process it failed.

topics.title: Sell-Side Process: Teaser, NDA & CIM
topics.description: What bankers actually produce between mandate and close, and how a buyer reads it: the anonymous teaser, the NDA, the CIM, the process letter and the buyer list.

steps.d: Teaser to NDA to CIM to bids — what each document is for and who sees it.
Read a real one and note what it asserts, what it omits, and why it never states a price.
Segment strategics vs sponsors for a target and justify the cut.

topics.title: Pitch Books
topics.description: What a pitch book is for and how it is assembled — situation overview, market update, valuation football field, and the recommendation the whole deck exists to support.

steps.d: Dissect a published pitch book and name what each section is doing.
Assemble a valuation range from DCF, comps and precedents.
Draft the recommendation page and make every prior slide support it.

topics.title: Merger Models & Accretion/Dilution
topics.description: Build a pro-forma EPS bridge: consideration mix, synergies, foregone interest and the break-even premium. The most-tested technical in an IB interview.

steps.d: Combine the two P&Ls, layer in the financing, and get to pro-forma EPS.
Solve for the premium at which the deal stops being accretive.
Rerun it as all-cash, all-stock and mixed; explain why the answer moves.

topics.title: Synergies & Post-Merger Integration
topics.description: Where the premium is supposed to come back from: cost and revenue synergies, how each is quantified and phased, and why integration is where most of the value is lost.

steps.d: Separate cost from revenue and say which one underwriters believe.
Put a number and a realisation timeline on three specific synergies.
Subtract integration costs and restate the premium the deal can bear.

topics.title: Equity & Debt Capital Markets
topics.description: How companies actually raise money: the IPO process end to end, follow-ons and convertibles on the equity side, investment-grade issuance on the debt side, and how ECM and DCM desks differ from M&A.

steps.d: Underwriter selection, S-1, roadshow, bookbuilding, pricing and the first day.
Pull one from EDGAR and find the risk factors, use of proceeds and dilution.
ECM vs DCM vs LevFin — who does what, and what the work looks like day to day.

topics.title: Private Equity Fundamentals
topics.description: How PE funds are structured (GP/LP, fees, carry), how they source and screen deals, and how a buyout thesis turns into an investment.

steps.d: GP versus LP, management fee, carry and the fund lifecycle.
Apply a buyout screen to a real company and pass or kill it.
State the entry case, the value-creation plan and the exit in one page.

topics.title: Fund Economics & Value Creation
topics.description: How a fund actually makes money and how returns get attributed: hurdle, catch-up, European vs American waterfall, and splitting an outcome into deleveraging, EBITDA growth and multiple expansion.

steps.d: Run an exit through European and American structures and compare GP take.
Decompose an IRR into deleveraging, earnings growth and multiple arbitrage.
Decide which lever did the work — and whether it was skill or the market.

topics.title: Hedge Fund Strategies
topics.description: Survey the core hedge fund strategies — long/short equity, global macro, quant, event-driven, arbitrage — and how each generates returns.

steps.d: Define long/short, macro, quant, event-driven and arbitrage by return source.
Name what each one is really exposed to.
Write a thesis, the catalyst and how you would size it.

topics.title: Venture Capital Basics
topics.description: How VC funds are structured and how they evaluate, price, and structure early-stage investments — from thesis to term sheet.

steps.d: Seed through Series C — who invests, what changes each time.
Work pre- and post-money, option pool and the founder dilution.
Find liquidation preference, participation and anti-dilution and say who they protect.

topics.title: Growth Equity & Secondaries
topics.description: The two private-equity adjacencies with their own recruiting tracks: growth equity's minority, low-leverage case study, and the secondaries market's pricing at a discount to NAV.

steps.d: Work cohort retention and unit economics on a real-shaped business.
Value it without leverage — the LBO maths does not apply.
Value an LP position at a discount to NAV and justify the discount.
Follow a GP-led secondary from motive to close.

topics.title: Leveraged Loans & High Yield
topics.description: The leveraged product set: term loan B versus senior notes, pricing and call protection, and the CLO and high-yield-fund buyer base that decides what can actually get financed.

steps.d: Term loan B vs senior notes: security, seniority, floating vs fixed, call protection.
Work out who buys each — CLOs, HY funds, direct lenders — and how that shapes terms.
Take a recent LBO and reason through why its capital structure was built the way it was.

topics.title: Restructuring & Chapter 11
topics.description: In-court versus out-of-court, creditor hierarchy and the absolute priority rule, DIP financing, liquidation analysis and the plan of reorganisation — plus how restructuring interviews differ from standard IB.

steps.d: Absolute priority rule: who gets paid, in what order, and where the fulcrum security sits.
Out-of-court exchange vs Chapter 11 — the trade-offs on speed, cost and holdouts.
Recovery by class, and what it implies for where value breaks.
Work the RX interview question set until the answers are yours.

topics.title: Private Credit & Direct Lending
topics.description: Non-bank lenders underwrite bilaterally and hold to maturity, so documentation and downside protection matter more than syndication flex. The fastest-growing seat in the market.

steps.d: Direct lending versus broadly syndicated leveraged finance.
Roll first and second lien into one tranche and price the all-in yield.
Model a case that trips a covenant and see what the lender can do.
Understand the BDC and fund structures behind the money.

topics.title: Distressed Debt & Event-Driven Investing
topics.description: Buying claims rather than advising on them. Find the fulcrum security, value the estate, and take a view on recovery or control — a different discipline from the restructuring advisory taught earlier.

steps.d: Locate the security that converts to equity in a reorganisation.
Price the claim, not the company — at a price, with a recovery view.
Run a recovery waterfall and the path to control.
Frame a catalyst and size a merger-arbitrage position.

topics.title: Options & Greeks Fundamentals
topics.description: How call and put options are priced, how payoff diagrams work, and how the Greeks — delta, gamma, theta, vega — measure each dimension of an option position's risk.

steps.d: Diagram long and short calls and puts at expiry.
Separate intrinsic from time value and see what moves each.
Show how delta, gamma, theta and vega each change a position's P&L.
Delta-hedge a position and explain why it needs re-hedging.

topics.title: Interest Rate & Credit Derivatives
topics.description: How interest rate swaps transfer rate risk between counterparties, and how credit default swaps transfer credit risk — the instruments at the heart of fixed-income and credit risk management.

steps.d: Build a fixed-for-floating swap and identify each leg's exposure.
Explain why a corporate borrower would enter one.
Price a CDS as insurance and define exactly what triggers a credit event.

topics.title: Securitization & ABS/MBS Basics
topics.description: How loans are pooled and tranched into asset-backed securities — the mechanics of cash-flow waterfalls, credit enhancement, and the key differences between ABS and MBS.

steps.d: Take a loan pool and cut it into senior, mezzanine and equity.
Allocate cash and losses through the stack in order.
Apply overcollateralisation and excess spread, then compare ABS to MBS.

topics.title: Risk, Capital & ALM
topics.description: The risk seat's own vocabulary: value at risk for market risk, risk-weighted assets and CET1 for capital, CVA for counterparty exposure, and EVE and NII for the banking book.

steps.d: Calculate it, then say plainly what it does not tell you.
Find RWA and CET1 in a real bank disclosure.
Understand CVA and why Basel III charged for it.
Work economic value of equity and net interest income sensitivity.

topics.title: FIG: Modelling Banks & Insurers
topics.description: Banks have no EBITDA and no free cash flow. You model the balance sheet first, drive earnings off net interest margin and provisions, and value on price-to-tangible-book and a dividend discount model.

steps.d: Start with assets and funding, not revenue.
Model net interest margin, provisions and regulatory capital.
Use P/TBV and DDM — EV/EBITDA is meaningless here.
Work tangible book dilution and the earn-back period.

topics.title: Real Estate Finance & REITs
topics.description: Property is valued on net operating income and a cap rate, not an EBITDA multiple. REITs report FFO and AFFO instead of EPS and trade at a premium or discount to net asset value.

steps.d: Build NOI, apply a cap rate, and get to an exit value.
Assemble a REIT net asset value and compare it to the share price.
Tie FFO, AFFO and CAD back to net income.
Work a JV equity promote between sponsor and investor.

topics.title: Project & Infrastructure Finance
topics.description: Non-recourse, single-asset financing sized off contracted cash flows. The model is a debt-sizing exercise around DSCR and LLCR inside an SPV, with no terminal value anywhere in it.

steps.d: Construct cash flow available for debt service for one asset.
Size and shape repayment to a target DSCR.
Work LLCR and the lender protections around it.
Say why corporate finance intuitions fail on a project.

topics.title: Earnings Quality & Accruals Analysis
topics.description: Assess whether reported earnings reflect real cash generation or aggressive accrual-accounting choices — the foundation of any forensic analysis.

steps.d: Put net income next to cash from operations over five years.
Compute the accrual ratio and flag the years it spikes.
Tie a spike to a specific policy or one-off and judge whether earnings are real.

topics.title: Off-Balance-Sheet Items & SPVs
topics.description: Identify leverage and commitments that do not appear on the balance sheet — operating leases, SPVs, synthetic securitizations — and understand when accounting standards require consolidation.

steps.d: Find commitments, guarantees and leases disclosed but not on the face.
Work out what it holds, who bears the risk, and whether it consolidates.
Add the off-balance-sheet items back and recompute the ratios.

topics.title: Red Flags in Financial Statements
topics.description: The warning signs that preceded Enron, WorldCom, and the 2008 crisis — rapidly growing receivables, channel stuffing, related-party transactions, and the Beneish M-Score manipulation detector.

steps.d: Receivables and inventory growing ahead of revenue, margin outliers, related parties.
Run a Beneish M-Score on one company and interpret the output.
Take Enron or WorldCom and mark which flags were visible in the last clean filing.

topics.title: Reading 10-Ks & 10-Qs
topics.description: Navigate a real 10-K and 10-Q section by section — MD&A, risk factors, the footnotes and the segment data — and pull the numbers a model actually needs out of a filing.

steps.d: Items 1, 1A, 7 and 8 — what each is for and what it hides.
Extract debt terms, leases, segments and share count.
Pull a filing into a driver sheet and reconcile every input to a page number.

topics.title: Deal Practice & Interview Prep
topics.description: Rehearse under deal conditions: paper LBOs, timed modelling tests, and the technical question set, until the reasoning is fast enough to survive an interview.

steps.d: Approximate IRR and MOIC with no spreadsheet, under time.
Run the timed LBO test, then diff your build against the solution.
Work the DCF, comps and accretion/dilution question sets until answers are yours.
Run one full interview out loud with someone else scoring.

topics.title: Indian Capital Markets, SEBI & Career Paths
topics.description: The regulatory and market architecture an analyst in India is actually asked about, plus an honest read on CFA versus CA versus FRM and where the Indian deal market hires.

steps.d: SEBI, NSE and BSE, the depositories and clearing corporations.
DRHP, book-building and the anchor book.
Indian investment banking and private equity, and who hires in Mumbai.
Pick between CFA, CA and FRM for the seat you actually want.

topics.title: Ratio Analysis & DuPont Decomposition
topics.description: Break return on equity into its profitability, efficiency and leverage drivers with DuPont analysis, and use the full ratio toolkit to judge a company's financial health.

steps.d: Calculate profitability, efficiency, liquidity and solvency ratios from one company's statements.
Split ROE into net margin, asset turnover and the equity multiplier with 3-step DuPont.
Take two years of the same company and say which DuPont driver moved ROE and why.

topics.title: Common-Size and Trend Analysis
topics.description: Normalize statements to a base (common-size/vertical analysis) and compare periods (horizontal/trend analysis) to spot structural shifts a raw dollar figure hides.

steps.d: Express every income statement line as a percent of revenue and every balance sheet line as a percent of assets.
Index 3-5 years of the same statement to a base year and compute period-over-period growth.
Identify one margin or mix change a peer comparison of common-size statements reveals.

topics.title: Cash Flow Analysis, Working Capital & the Cash Conversion Cycle
topics.description: Analyze how efficiently a company turns sales into cash: working capital mechanics, and the cash conversion cycle as the standard lens on that efficiency.

steps.d: Calculate DIO, DSO and DPO for a real company and combine them into the cash conversion cycle.
Compare that cycle against a close peer and identify which leg drives the difference.
Show how a one-day change in DSO moves free cash flow.

topics.title: Budgeting Approaches & the Annual Planning Cycle
topics.description: Understand how companies build an annual budget, the main budgeting methods and their trade-offs, and how actuals get checked against plan.

steps.d: Lay out the steps from target-setting through budget committee approval.
Contrast incremental, zero-based and activity-based budgeting on effort versus control.
Compute a budget-to-actual variance and classify it as favorable or unfavorable.

topics.title: 13-Week and Monthly Cash-Flow Forecasting
topics.description: Build short-term liquidity forecasts the way treasury and FP&A teams actually run them: the direct-method 13-week rolling forecast and the monthly indirect-method view.

steps.d: Lay out weekly cash inflows and outflows with the direct method and roll it forward one week.
Forecast a monthly cash flow model over a 12-18 month rolling horizon.
Flex a collections assumption and see how many weeks of runway change.

topics.title: Scenario & Sensitivity Analysis
topics.description: Test which assumptions actually move a model's output using Excel data tables and a scenario manager, and present the results so a decision-maker can act on them.

steps.d: Sensitize one output to two input variables with a two-variable data table.
Define base, upside and downside cases in a scenario manager.
Identify which two assumptions move the output the most.

topics.title: Model Structure, Design & Best Practices
topics.description: Learn the conventions that make a model intuitive and error-resistant: consistent formatting, separating inputs from calculations from outputs, and documenting assumptions.

steps.d: Rebuild a messy model into distinct assumptions, calculation and output sheets.
Color hardcodes blue and formulas black, and label every unit and time period.
Write a one-line rationale next to each hardcoded driver.

topics.title: Driver-Based Forecasting: Revenue & Cost Builds
topics.description: Forecast revenue and cost of goods sold from operating drivers (price, volume, mix) rather than a flat growth rate, and know when a bottom-up build is worth the extra effort.

steps.d: Decompose revenue into price and volume for one segment.
Forecast three years of revenue and COGS from unit economics rather than a growth assumption.
Cross-check the bottom-up build against a simple growth-rate forecast.

topics.title: Supporting Schedules: PP&E, Working Capital, Debt & Equity
topics.description: Build the schedules that feed a 3-statement model: a PP&E roll-forward, working-capital and balance-sheet line forecasts, and a debt schedule with interest and mandatory repayments.

steps.d: Link beginning balance, capex and depreciation into an ending balance.
Project working-capital and other balance-sheet lines off their own drivers.
Lay out each tranche's balance, interest and scheduled amortization.

topics.title: Circularity, Balancing & Model Auditing
topics.description: Understand why circular references appear once debt and interest are linked together, how to handle them safely, and how to audit a finished model for errors before anyone relies on it.

steps.d: Link interest expense to average debt and watch the circular reference appear.
Build an error-trap toggle that can turn iterative calculation on and off.
Run a formula-error and formatting pass over a finished model before sign-off.

topics.title: EV-to-Equity Bridge & the Treasury Stock Method
topics.description: Bridge enterprise value to equity value correctly, and use the treasury stock method to convert dilutive options and warrants into a fully diluted share count.

steps.d: Subtract net debt, preferred stock and minority interest from enterprise value to reach equity value.
Compute the net new shares from in-the-money options assuming proceeds buy back shares.
Divide equity value by fully diluted shares to get value per share.

topics.title: Terminal Value, Mid-Year Convention & Stub Periods
topics.description: Choose between the Gordon growth and exit multiple terminal value methods, cross-check one against the other, and apply mid-year discounting and stub periods without silently mixing conventions.

steps.d: Calculate terminal value with Gordon growth and with an exit multiple, and cross-check them.
Halve the first period's discount factor and adjust every later period by 0.5.
Discount a first-year cash flow that covers less than a full 12 months correctly.

topics.title: Valuation Synthesis: the Football Field
topics.description: Bring DCF, comps and precedent transactions together into a single football field chart that shows the range and the overlap across methods.

steps.d: Pull the low/high value range from each valuation method you've built.
Lay the ranges out as horizontal bars on a shared value-per-share axis.
Identify where the ranges converge and what that implies about the valuation.

topics.title: Data Visualization Principles for Financial Reporting
topics.description: Choose the right chart for the message, and apply the principles that make a financial visual persuasive rather than merely decorative.

steps.d: Pick the chart type that fits a trend, a comparison and a composition question.
Strip a cluttered chart down to the data that supports its one point.
Build a single KPI tile with a clear label, value and trend indicator.

topics.title: Building Interactive Finance Dashboards in Excel
topics.description: Build a working Excel dashboard with pivot tables, slicers and sparklines that lets a viewer explore variance without touching a formula.

steps.d: Set up the pivot tables that will power every chart and KPI card.
Wire up slicers so one control filters every chart on the dashboard.
Drop in-cell sparklines next to a KPI table to show its recent trend.

topics.title: Financial Storytelling & Data Narrative
topics.description: Turn a set of numbers into a structured narrative that leads an audience from context to insight to recommended action.

steps.d: Write the one-sentence conclusion before building the supporting slides.
Sequence context, insight and recommendation using a repeatable framework.
Rewrite a data-dense slide so its title states the takeaway, not the topic.

topics.title: Business & Financial Writing
topics.description: Write the memo, executive summary or email that gets a busy reader to the decision quickly: lead with the conclusion, and cut every sentence that doesn't earn its place.

steps.d: Rewrite a memo so its first line states the conclusion, not the background.
Halve a paragraph's word count without losing its meaning.
Write a one-page executive summary for a business plan or proposal.

topics.title: Presenting Finance to Leadership & Building the Deck
topics.description: Structure a management presentation the way a finance team actually builds one, and use PowerPoint efficiently enough to iterate under deadline pressure.

steps.d: Lay out a presentation from problem through methodology to financial implications and recommendation.
Apply keyboard-driven PowerPoint techniques to reformat a slide in under a minute.
Present the deck's key slide out loud and time it to under two minutes.

topics.title: Acquisition Underwriting: Income Capitalization & Pro Forma
topics.description: Go beyond the REIT-level FFO/AFFO view (fin-p14-t2) into deal-level underwriting: build a property-level pro forma and value it off NOI and a market cap rate the way an acquisitions analyst does.

steps.d: Work through A.CRE's walkthrough of Value = NOI ÷ Cap Rate and rebuild it on a simple rent roll.

steps.t: Read Damodaran's real estate valuation chapter
steps.d: Note where DCF-based property valuation agrees with, and departs from, cap-rate shorthand.

steps.t: Build a full property pro forma
steps.d: Follow the BIWS walkthrough to construct revenue, vacancy, opex and NOI lines for an office or multifamily asset.

steps.t: Underwrite a deal end to end
steps.d: Use the free Ai1 model to underwrite one acquisition and one development scenario, and compare the assumptions each requires.

topics.title: Debt Sizing & Real Estate Equity Waterfalls
topics.description: Size acquisition debt the way a CRE lender does (DSCR, debt yield, loan constant), then build the promote structure that splits a deal's profit between the sponsor and LP investors across return tiers.

steps.d: Work the PropertyMetrics DSCR walkthrough and back into a maximum loan amount from a target coverage ratio.
Recompute the same loan's size using the debt yield method and compare the two constraints.
Work through Break Into CRE's guide to see how preferred return, catch-up and promote tiers stack.
Follow the Adventures in CRE model and video to build IRR-hurdle-based waterfall tiers in Excel and test how promote changes with hold period.

topics.title: Ground-Up Development: Land Residual & Construction Pro Forma
topics.description: Model a development deal from raw land: back into a maximum land price with a residual land value analysis, then build the construction-phase cash flow and lease-up that feeds the stabilized pro forma.

steps.d: Follow the A.CRE walkthrough to back a maximum land bid out of projected sellout value, hard/soft costs and required developer profit.
Add a construction draw schedule and lease-up curve ahead of the stabilized NOI you built in t1.

steps.t: Watch a full development model build
steps.d: Follow the multifamily development walkthrough end to end and note every line item you have not yet built yourself.
Flex construction cost overruns and a slower lease-up in your model and see how much they move the developer's profit and IRR.

topics.title: Mining Valuation: Reserves Classification, NAV & Price Decks
topics.description: Mining assets are valued by summing the discounted cash flows of each individual mine (a NAV, sum-of-the-parts approach), driven off reserve/resource classification and a metal price deck rather than a revenue multiple.

steps.d: Read CFI's overview of mining asset valuation and note why P/NAV, not a revenue multiple, is the standard trading metric.
Read through NI 43-101's measured/indicated/inferred resource and reserve categories and why 'inferred' cannot be used in an economic study.
Work through the guide on mining NAV, reserve life and commodity sensitivity, and note how mine life caps the DCF horizon.
Follow the in-depth mining financial model walkthrough and rebuild its production, cost and NAV tabs for one commodity.

topics.title: Oil & Gas Modelling: Decline Curves, Type Curves & NAV
topics.description: An E&P company's production declines to zero as its wells deplete, so revenue is modelled off a decline curve rather than a growth assumption, and the company is valued as a NAV of its existing and type-curve-driven future wells.

steps.d: Follow the BIWS NAV model video to build annual production off an assumed decline rate for a single well.

steps.t: Apply a type curve to new wells
steps.d: Work through the type-curve tutorial to see how a new well's expected production profile is used to model undrilled locations.
Use the crash-course Excel files to build out an E&P NAV model combining existing production and type-curve-driven new wells.

steps.t: Read why NAV, not DCF-to-infinity, is used
steps.d: Read the energy NAV explainer and write one paragraph on why terminal value has no place in this model.

topics.title: Commodity Price Decks & Sensitivity Analysis
topics.description: The commodity price deck is usually the single most debated input in a natural-resources model, so build the scenario structure (strip, consensus, management, bull/bear) and the two-way sensitivity tables that stress-test it.

steps.d: Read how energy bankers build strip, consensus-deck, management-case and bull/bear price scenarios into one model.
Read the forward curve reference and note how strip pricing is derived from futures contracts rather than assumed.
Follow the Wall Street Prep sensitivity lesson to build a two-way Excel data table flexing price and discount rate against NAV.

steps.t: Re-run your mining or O&G NAV under three decks
steps.d: Rerun the model you built in t1 or t2 under a bull, base and bear price deck and report how much NAV moves.

topics.title: Renewable Power Project Modelling: PPA & Capacity Factor
topics.description: A solar or wind project's revenue is production (driven by capacity factor) times a contracted PPA price, not a market-priced merchant curve, which is what lets it be financed with cheap, highly-levered non-recourse debt.

steps.d: Read how a renewable project's model differs from a merchant gas plant's: PPA-fixed price times production, plus tax credits.
Read the EIA definition and note why a 30% solar capacity factor still supports a highly-levered financing.

steps.t: Read how financial PPAs are structured
steps.d: Work through EPA's explainer on financial (virtual) PPAs and how the strike-price swap hedges the generator's revenue.
Download one of Edward Bodmer's solar project finance models and trace production, PPA revenue and debt service through to equity IRR.

topics.title: Advanced Project Finance: CFADS & Debt Sculpting
topics.description: Go beyond the single DSCR/LLCR sizing pass in fin-p14-t3: build Cash Flow Available for Debt Service (CFADS) precisely, then sculpt principal repayment period by period so the DSCR sits exactly at its covenant floor across the loan life.

steps.t: Build CFADS from the cash flow statement
steps.d: Follow the BIWS tutorial to strip a project's cash flow down to CFADS, distinct from EBITDA or free cash flow.
Work through the debt-sculpting-vs-sizing tutorial and note why a sculpted repayment profile is not the same as a level amortization schedule.

steps.t: Sculpt debt service to a target DSCR
steps.d: Follow the Forvis Mazars walkthrough to build a sculpted debt schedule that holds DSCR at its minimum every period without a circular VBA macro.

steps.t: Extend to multiple tranches and a DSRA
steps.d: Work through Bodmer's sculpting course materials to add a debt service reserve account and see how sculpting changes with two debt tranches.

topics.title: Infrastructure & PPP Modelling
topics.description: Public infrastructure that has no user-fee revenue of its own (a courthouse, a school) is financed instead against a government's availability payment, a fixed obligation once the asset is certified ready for use.

steps.t: Read the PPP handbook's financing chapter
steps.d: Read ADB's PPP handbook section on how a concession is financed and what risks are transferred to the private partner.
Work through the APMG explainer on availability payments and how they differ from a toll or user-fee concession.

steps.t: Read a real-world availability payment fact sheet
steps.d: Read FHWA's fact sheet on availability payment P3s and note why lenders accept lower rates on this structure.

steps.t: Compare the three project finance structures
steps.d: Write one paragraph contrasting the renewable PPA project (t1), a merchant/sculpted debt deal (t2) and an availability-payment PPP on what backs the debt.

topics.title: SaaS & Tech: Cohort Analysis, Unit Economics & ARR
topics.description: Model a subscription business off ARR, cohort-level retention and the LTV/CAC relationship rather than a traditional revenue build, and know which multiple (ARR vs. revenue) the market actually prices it on.

steps.d: Work through David Skok's SaaS Metrics 2.0 definitions for MRR, ARR, churn, CAC and LTV.
Follow ChartMogul's cohort analysis walkthrough and build a cohort-by-tenure retention grid in a spreadsheet.

steps.t: Build a full SaaS metrics model
steps.d: Follow the BIWS video and Excel example to model ARR, CAC payback and the LTV/CAC ratio together.
Read Wall Street Prep's ARR multiple lesson and note why SaaS companies are priced on ARR rather than trailing revenue.

topics.title: E-Commerce & Marketplace Revenue Modelling
topics.description: A marketplace's real top line is GMV, not revenue: model gross merchandise volume, the take rate that converts it into revenue, and liquidity — and know why quoting GMV as revenue overstates the business.

steps.d: Read a16z's 13 metrics for marketplace companies and separate GMV from revenue in your head permanently.

steps.t: Learn the broader startup metric set
steps.d: Read a16z's 16 startup metrics to place marketplace-specific metrics alongside general SaaS/e-commerce ones.

steps.t: Read how young growth companies get valued
steps.d: Work through Damodaran's chapter on valuing young or start-up firms and note how a market-size-down revenue build feeds a DCF with almost no current revenue.
In a spreadsheet, build GMV growth, apply a take rate, and bridge to net revenue and contribution margin for a hypothetical marketplace.

topics.title: Consumer, Retail & Restaurant Unit Economics
topics.description: Chains are valued store by store: same-store sales isolates organic growth from new-unit growth, and four-wall economics and payback period decide whether opening the next unit creates value.

steps.d: Read CFI's explainer and compute a comp-sales figure that excludes stores open under 12 months.
Read the QSR unit economics explainer and compute four-wall EBITDA margin from a sample P&L.
Use the Wall Street Prep payback period lesson to compute how many years a new store or restaurant takes to repay its build-out cost.
Combine same-store sales growth with a new-unit build schedule to project a growing chain's system-wide revenue.

topics.title: Healthcare & Biotech: rNPV and Pipeline Valuation
topics.description: A clinical-stage biotech has no revenue and a high chance of failure, so its pipeline is valued with risk-adjusted NPV: probability-weight each drug's cash flows by phase before discounting, rather than assuming they arrive with certainty.

steps.d: Read the core explainer on why clinical risk is probability-weighted separately from financial (discount-rate) risk.
Read BIO's clinical development success rates report and pull the phase-to-phase transition probabilities it reports by therapeutic area.
Follow the BayBridge Bio walkthrough to build a single asset's rNPV: peak sales, phase-by-phase PoS, and a low discount rate on the risk-adjusted cash flows.
Extend your one-drug rNPV to three assets at different phases and sum them into one pipeline value.

topics.title: Full LBO Build: Sources & Uses to Returns Attribution
topics.description: Go past the single-tranche LBO in fin-p8-t2 into what a real deal looks like: a multi-tranche debt stack with different pricing and amortization on each piece, and a formal returns-attribution bridge that decomposes IRR into deleveraging, EBITDA growth and multiple expansion.

steps.t: Rebuild the cash sweep in detail
steps.d: Follow the full cash-flow-sweep tutorial and extend your fin-p8-t2 model to sweep multiple tranches in seniority order.
Complete Wall Street Prep's advanced LBO modeling test end to end under time pressure, matching what a PE associate interview actually looks like.
Read how deleveraging, EBITDA growth and multiple expansion typically split a deal's return, and why debt paydown alone can produce a real IRR.
Follow the CFI walkthrough to decompose your advanced LBO's equity value creation into the three levers and chart the bridge.

topics.title: Paper LBO & Quick IRR Math
topics.description: A PE interview routinely asks for an LBO's IRR with no Excel and five minutes: build the mental-math shortcuts (Rule of 72/115) that get you a Sources & Uses table and an approximate return in your head.

steps.t: Work through a full paper LBO example
steps.d: Follow the BIWS paper LBO walkthrough end to end without opening a spreadsheet.
Read the Rule of 72/115 framework and practice converting a MOIC and holding period into an approximate IRR in under 10 seconds.
Use the free paper LBO template to run 5 practice scenarios back to back, timing yourself under 5 minutes each.

steps.t: Check your math against a real model
steps.d: Take one scenario and build it properly in Excel from t1's structure, and compare your paper answer to the exact IRR.

topics.title: Advanced Merger Model: PPA & Pro-Forma Balance Sheet
topics.description: Extend the accretion/dilution model in fin-p5-t3 with purchase price allocation: revalue the target's assets to fair value, calculate the resulting goodwill, and consolidate both companies' balance sheets on day one.

steps.d: Read Wall Street Prep's walkthrough of allocating purchase price across tangible assets, identifiable intangibles and goodwill.
Follow the BIWS video and Excel example to calculate write-ups, deferred tax liabilities and resulting goodwill for one deal.
Follow Macabacus's PPA guide to combine acquirer and target balance sheets into one pro-forma day-one balance sheet.

steps.t: Feed PPA back into your merger model
steps.d: Add the new D&A from write-ups and the new goodwill into the EPS accretion/dilution model from fin-p5-t3 and see how much it changes the result.

topics.title: Contribution Analysis, SOTP & Fairness Opinions
topics.description: Round out the deal-modelling toolkit with the frameworks used on complex or contested transactions: contribution analysis to set ownership splits in a merger of equals, sum-of-the-parts to value a conglomerate, and the fairness opinion a board relies on to approve a deal.

steps.d: Follow Macabacus's example to compute each company's percentage contribution to combined revenue, EBITDA and net income, and compare it to the proposed ownership split.
Read the SOTP methodology guide and value a hypothetical multi-segment company by valuing and summing each segment separately.

steps.t: Learn what a fairness opinion actually says
steps.d: Read CFI's overview and note precisely what question a fairness opinion answers, and what it deliberately does not answer.
Read the M&I guide on fairness opinions, including how banks are paid for them and the conflicts that raises.

topics.title: Fund Cash Flow Modelling: Capital Calls & the J-Curve
topics.description: Build the fund-level cash flow model itself, not just the waterfall concepts in fin-p9-t4: a commitment-pacing schedule, capital calls, fee accrual and distributions that together produce the fund's characteristic J-shaped cash flow curve.

steps.d: Read Wall Street Prep's explanation of why fees and early capital calls make early fund years look negative.
Read Hamilton Lane's introduction to J-curves and note how they discuss flattening it across a portfolio of fund vintages.
Follow the walkthrough of capital calls, distributions and the J-curve to lay out a commitment-pacing tab, a fee-accrual tab and a distribution tab.
Build a 10-year capital call and distribution schedule for a hypothetical fund and chart cumulative net cash flow to see the J shape emerge.

topics.title: Return Metrics: IRR vs MOIC vs DPI/TVPI
topics.description: Calculate the four numbers every LP asks a GP for, and know when each one is the right answer: IRR (time-weighted), MOIC (magnitude only), and DPI/TVPI (cash returned vs. total value, realized vs. unrealized).

steps.d: Work the Wall Street Prep MOIC lesson and compute it for a simple two-cash-flow investment.
Follow the BIWS walkthrough and confirm for yourself that TVPI = DPI + RVPI on a sample fund.
Read Carta's overview of fund performance metrics and note which metric LPs weight most heavily at different points in a fund's life.
Add IRR, MOIC, DPI and TVPI formulas to the cash flow model from t1 and track how each evolves year by year.

topics.title: Cap Tables, Dilution & Liquidation Preferences
topics.description: Go past the thesis-and-term-sheet view in fin-p9-t3 into the actual math: build a cap table across financing rounds, calculate dilution including the option pool shuffle, and model how a liquidation preference stack pays out at exit.

steps.d: Follow Carta's cap table explainer and lay out founders, an option pool and one priced round with ownership percentages.
Read CRV's dilution guide and recompute your cap table's founder ownership with the pool created pre-money vs. post-money.
Follow the guide on modelling liquidation preferences to add 1x non-participating preferred stock to your cap table.
Follow Carta's waterfall analysis guide to calculate each shareholder's payout at three different exit values, including where the preference stops binding.

topics.title: Revenue Recognition (ASC 606 / IFRS 15)
topics.description: The five-step model that now governs revenue recognition under both US GAAP and IFRS — identifying the contract and performance obligations, pricing them, and timing recognition to when control transfers, not when cash is collected.

steps.d: Work through contract, performance obligations, transaction price, allocation and recognition in order.
Skim the IFRS 15 core principle and see how closely it mirrors ASC 606.
Take a multi-element contract (software plus support) and split the transaction price across obligations.
Identify where management discretion over timing or allocation could move reported revenue.

topics.title: Leases (ASC 842 / IFRS 16)
topics.description: Since 2019 almost every lease sits on the balance sheet as a right-of-use asset and a lease liability. Learn the classification test, the journal entries, and why finance and operating leases still hit the income statement differently under US GAAP.

steps.d: Run a lease through the finance-vs-operating test under ASC 842.
Record the initial right-of-use asset and lease liability at present value.
Amortise a finance lease and straight-line an operating lease and compare the expense patterns.
Note that IFRS 16 drops the lessee operating-lease category entirely and say what that does to EBITDA.

topics.title: Deferred Tax, NOLs & Stock-Based Compensation
topics.description: Three line items that separate GAAP earnings from cash and from each other: the deferred tax assets and liabilities that arise when book and tax timing diverge, the NOLs a loss-making company carries forward, and the non-cash stock compensation expense that dilutes shareholders without ever touching cash flow.

steps.d: Take one timing difference (depreciation or an accrual) and compute the resulting deferred tax balance.
Walk a loss through a valuation allowance and into future tax savings.
Recognise stock-based compensation over a vesting schedule and trace it through the cash flow statement add-back.
Connect SBC to the diluted share count a model should be forecasting.

topics.title: Consolidation, NCI & the Equity Method
topics.description: Three ways to account for an equity stake depending on control: cost method below 20%, equity method for 20-50% influence, and full consolidation with a non-controlling interest line above 50%. Get the thresholds and the mechanics of each.

steps.d: Map ownership percentage to cost, equity-method and consolidation treatment.
Roll a one-line equity-method investment forward through income, dividends and impairment.
Combine 100% of a partly-owned subsidiary's statements and carve out the NCI.
Find non-controlling interest in a filing and say what it implies about the parent's actual claim on earnings.

topics.title: Goodwill, Purchase Price Allocation & Impairment
topics.description: What happens to the balance sheet the day after an acquisition closes: fair-valuing the target's assets, booking the residual as goodwill, and testing that goodwill for impairment every year after.

steps.d: Fair-value tangible and intangible assets acquired and compute the goodwill residual.
Schedule the new intangible assets PPA creates and their effect on post-deal EPS.
Run a qualitative screen, then a quantitative fair-value test on a goodwill balance.
Find a disclosed goodwill impairment and identify the triggering event management cited.

topics.title: Pensions & Post-Employment Benefits
topics.description: Defined benefit plans put a long-dated, discount-rate-sensitive liability on the balance sheet and a multi-part expense on the income statement — service cost, interest cost, and the return on plan assets, all before a single benefit is paid.

steps.d: Contrast defined contribution and defined benefit obligations.
Assemble pension expense from service cost, interest cost and expected return on assets.
Move the discount rate and see the obligation and expense both move.
Locate a company's pension funded status in its footnotes and say what it means for future cash contributions.

topics.title: IFRS vs US GAAP vs Ind AS
topics.description: The framework differences that matter for cross-border comparability: LIFO, development-cost capitalisation, cash flow classification, and the specific carve-outs India's Ind AS makes from the IFRS it is based on.

steps.d: Name the inventory, development-cost and cash-flow-classification differences between GAAP and IFRS.
Adjust a GAAP company's operating cash flow to an IFRS peer's classification convention.
Identify two areas where Ind AS carves out from the IFRS standard it is based on.
Decide whether a cross-border comp set needs restating before you trust the multiples.

topics.title: Bond Pricing, Yields & the Yield Curve
topics.description: A bond's price is the present value of its coupons and principal at the market yield. Learn to price a bond from its cash flows, read yield to maturity as an IRR, and plot the yield curve that every other rate in the market is set relative to.

steps.d: Discount a bond's coupons and principal at a given yield to get its price.
Go the other way — take a market price and solve for the yield that produces it.
Chart yields across maturities and name the shape — normal, flat, inverted.
Explain what an inverted curve is telling the market about future rates.

topics.title: Duration, Convexity & Interest Rate Risk
topics.description: Duration approximates how much a bond's price moves for a 1% change in rates; convexity corrects for the fact that relationship curves rather than moves in a straight line. Together they are how a fixed-income desk sizes interest-rate risk.

steps.d: Calculate duration for a bond and use it to estimate a price move from a rate change.
Layer the convexity adjustment on top and see the estimate improve for a larger rate move.
Take a short- and long-maturity bond and explain why their durations differ so much.
Size a rate hedge using dollar duration on a small bond portfolio.

topics.title: Credit Spreads & Relative Value
topics.description: The spread over a government benchmark is the market's price for a bond's default risk. Learn to read spread levels and spread widening or tightening as a signal, and how a credit investor decides one bond is cheap relative to another.

steps.d: Decompose a corporate bond's yield into a benchmark rate plus a credit spread.
Rank several issuers' spreads and connect the ranking to their credit quality.
Explain what widening spreads across the market are signalling versus one issuer alone.
Pick the richer of two similar bonds on a spread basis and justify the call.

topics.title: Credit Rating Methodology & the Rating Scale
topics.description: What AAA through D actually mean, and how an agency gets from a company's financials to a letter grade — the scorecard, the qualitative overlay, and the investment-grade/speculative-grade line that decides who is allowed to buy the bond.

steps.d: Map the AAA-to-D scale to investment grade versus speculative grade for one agency.
Read how a rating agency's scorecard weighs size, leverage and business risk into a rating.
Say why crossing from BBB- to BB+ triggers forced selling by some institutional holders.
Apply a simplified scorecard to a real issuer and compare your rating to the agency's.

topics.title: Loan & Credit Agreement Mechanics
topics.description: What is actually in the document that governs a loan: maintenance versus incurrence covenants, why cov-lite structures shifted market power to borrowers, and what a lender can and cannot do when a covenant is breached.

steps.d: Distinguish maintenance covenants (tested every quarter) from incurrence covenants (tested on an action).
Explain why cov-lite loans shifted negotiating leverage from lenders to sponsors.
Trace what happens contractually the moment a maintenance covenant is breached.
Skim a real credit agreement's table of contents and locate the covenants and events-of-default sections.

topics.title: Forwards, Futures & Cost-of-Carry Pricing
topics.description: Why a forward or futures price is what it is: the no-arbitrage relationship between spot price, the cost of financing and holding the underlying, and any income it throws off in between.

steps.d: Add financing cost and subtract any yield on the underlying to get from spot to forward price.
Show what a cash-and-carry trade earns if the market price deviates from the theoretical forward.
Apply the interest-rate-differential version of the formula to an FX forward.
Explain what daily marking-to-market and exchange clearing change versus an OTC forward.

topics.title: Swap Valuation
topics.description: How the fixed and floating legs of an interest rate swap are each valued as a bond, why the swap is worth zero at inception, and how its mark-to-market value moves as rates move afterward.

steps.d: Discount the fixed coupon stream at the swap curve to get its present value.
Show why the floating leg reprices to par at each reset and what that implies for its value.
Combine both legs into the swap's mark-to-market value from the payer's side.
Shift rates after inception and recompute the swap's now-nonzero value.

topics.title: Option Pricing: Binomial Trees & Black-Scholes
topics.description: The two ways an option actually gets priced: a discrete binomial lattice that a spreadsheet can build step by step, and the closed-form Black-Scholes formula the lattice converges to as the steps shrink.

steps.d: Price a single-period binomial option using the up/down replicating portfolio.
Add steps and watch the binomial price converge toward the Black-Scholes value.
Price a European call from spot, strike, volatility, rate and time to expiry.
Flex volatility and time and see which Greek each move is really testing.

topics.title: Real Options in Capital Budgeting
topics.description: A standard NPV ignores the value of managerial flexibility. Real options — to defer, expand, contract or abandon a project — apply option-pricing logic to that flexibility, and can make an uncertain project more valuable, not less.

steps.d: Distinguish the option to defer, expand, contract and abandon a project.
Explain why higher volatility raises a real option's value when it lowers a plain NPV.
Price the option to expand a project using a simplified binomial framework.
Compare a project's static NPV to its expanded NPV-plus-option-value and say which one should drive the decision.

topics.title: Cash & Liquidity Management
topics.description: Treasury's daily job: make sure cash is in the right entity, the right currency and the right account to meet every obligation that falls due, while putting idle cash to short-term use.

steps.d: Distinguish being profitable from being liquid and say why the second one keeps a company alive.
Roll up cash across accounts and entities into a single daily position.
Forecast a rolling liquidity runway and identify the first quarter it gets tight.
Choose a short-term investment ladder for cash not needed within the runway.

topics.title: FX Exposure & Hedging
topics.description: A company that sells or sources across currencies is short or long FX whether it hedges or not. Learn to separate transaction, translation and economic exposure, and hedge the one that actually threatens cash flow.

steps.d: Sort a multinational's currency risk into transaction, translation and economic exposure.
Lock in a receivable's value with a forward contract and compute the hedged outcome.
Explain why translation exposure is non-cash and decide whether it is worth hedging at all.
Write a simple policy for what share of 12-month exposure gets hedged and with what instrument.

topics.title: Interest Rate Risk Management for Corporates
topics.description: A borrower with floating-rate debt is exposed to rising rates; one with fixed-rate debt is exposed to being stuck above market if rates fall. Learn how corporates use swaps and caps to manage that trade-off.

steps.d: State what rising and falling rates each do to a floating-rate borrower's interest expense.
Convert floating-rate debt to fixed with a payer swap and recompute the all-in cost.

topics.title: CAPM, Factor Models & the Efficient Frontier

steps.d: Combine two risky assets across weights and trace out the risk-return curve.
Reduce the frontier's insight to a single beta against the market under CAPM.
Layer size and value factors onto CAPM and see how much more return variation they explain.

topics.title: Asset Allocation & Performance Attribution

topics.title: Regression & Statistical Methods for Finance

topics.title: Monte Carlo Simulation, VaR/ES & Stress Testing
